why.title: Audience check in token validation

github.title: Add audience validation to token verification
github.detail: Merged 2026-07-19. Adds the audience option to jwt.verify and the EXPECTED_AUD config.

github.title: fix(auth): reject tokens issued for other services
github.detail: Commit that introduced `audience: EXPECTED_AUD` (git blame, L21).

github.title: Set clockTolerance to 5s
github.detail: Added during the jwt 4.3 regression workaround.

jira.title: Tokens accepted without audience check
jira.detail: A token minted for notifications was accepted by payments, allowing cross-service replay. Done.

jira.title: Pin jwt library after 4.3 regression
jira.detail: Temporary workaround; related to the clock tolerance.

confluence.title: § Token validation
confluence.detail: Every service must verify `aud`. The gateway terminates TLS only.

narrative: This `audience` option exists because of AUTH-311: a token issued for another service was accepted by payments, which allowed cross-service replay. PR #377 added the check and the Authentication architecture page now requires every service to verify `aud`.
The `clockTolerance: 5` line is unrelated to security intent. It came later (PR #402) as part of the jwt 4.3 regression workaround tracked in AUTH-298.

why.title: Balance read straight from the ledger

github.title: Serve balance reads from the ledger only
github.detail: Merged 2026-09-04. Removes the short-lived balance cache.

github.title: revert: remove balance cache
github.detail: Reverts the caching layer (git blame, L7–L11).

jira.title: Stale balance shown after concurrent debit
jira.detail: Cache returned an old balance for up to 30s after a debit. Done.

jira.title: Investigate read latency on balance endpoint
jira.detail: Open. Latency complaints that motivate caching again.

confluence.title: § Reads
confluence.detail: Balances must be strongly consistent with the ledger.

narrative: The balance is read directly from PostgreSQL because a short-lived cache produced stale balances after concurrent debits (PAY-142). PR #318 removed the cache, and the Payments consistency model requires balance reads to be strongly consistent.
PAY-171 is still open: latency on this endpoint is the pressure to add caching again.

why.title: Serializable ledger transaction

github.title: Double-entry ledger in one serializable transaction

jira.title: Stale balance shown after concurrent debit
jira.detail: Concurrent debits are what exposed the race.

confluence.title: § Writes
confluence.detail: Debit, credit and entry insert commit atomically.

narrative: Both account updates and the entry insert run in one SERIALIZABLE transaction so concurrent debits cannot corrupt balances. This is the write-side counterpart of the strongly consistent reads described in the consistency model.

why.title: Centralized authorization middleware
narrative: Authorization used to be re-implemented in each service. PR #482 centralized it so policy changes happen in one place, and the conventions page asks every new endpoint to mount `authorizeRequest`.

why.title: Gateway routes without validating tokens

github.title: Gateway: routing and rate limiting only

jira.title: Evaluate JWT validation at the edge
jira.detail: Open. Blocked on per-route audience configuration.

confluence.title: § Responsibilities
confluence.detail: Gateway terminates TLS, routes and rate-limits.

narrative: The gateway deliberately skips token validation: it only routes and rate-limits, and each downstream service validates tokens itself (including the audience check from AUTH-311). PLAT-88 tracks evaluating edge validation, which is blocked on per-route audience configuration.
